newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy stock market 97 rise seen selective.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy stock market 97 rise seen selective.

text.p: The Italian stock market is expected to rise an average of 10-15 percent in 1997, but the increase in individual stocks will be selective, a Reuters survey of analysts and equity stategists showed.
They see the Milan stock market Comit index rising towards 710-725 by the end of 1997 from Monday's Comit close of 643.83. This index is based on a value of 100 for 1972.

Analysts expect investors to favour telecommunications and utility stocks and also energy giant ENI ; to snub banking and insurance shares, while industrial stocks will depend on the progress of the Italian economy.

Some analysts see a strong push from more privatisation issues and a fall in interest rates, while others are more cautious about the uncertainties facing the market. But all agree the market will be selective and will not show an overall boom.

Among the most optimistic is Carlo Capotorti, head of research at brokers Centrosim, who sees a rise of 15 percent during 1997 and expects company performances to be in line with those seen in other nations.

Italian savings bank Cariplo forecasts a good performance from the Milan bourse in 1997, which it sees as currently undervalued, and expects the Comit index to move towards 740-750 within six to eight months.

Michele Pezzinga at brokers Eptasim sees a better than average rise in the Comit index and forecasts up to 780. He adds that, with yields on money products at only a little over one percent a quarter, funds will tend to move towards products with greater risks, but with a better performance.

The head of research at broker IMI Sigeco Giampaolo Trasi and Paolo Toschi at Milla Sim forecast an average gain in the bourse of 10-15 percent in 1997 and sees an increased flow of managed funds into the equity market.

Less optimistic is Roberto Condulmari, head of research at broker Giubergia Warburg, who sees "an economy in great difficulty, at least for the first six months, with the possibility of earnings downgrades for many companies."
He added that, for industries suffering from the weak economy and strong lira, a fall in Italian interest rates will not compensate for the weakness of the economic environment.
Among sectors, analysts like telecoms, but many were also backing utilities and ENI.

One analyst at broker Comit said that, in the first half of the year, telecoms and utilities will likely be attractive, but in the second half, others such as Parmalat and Pirelli could emerge. The analyst was staying neutral on Fiat
